summary: PWA installability verification for GAWAD NET (users + /mof30 admin). All PWA assets serve HTTP 200 with correct content-types and valid JSON. index.html contains RTL <html lang=ar dir=rtl>, theme-color #221340, manifest link, apple-touch-icon links, and a navigator.serviceWorker.register('/service-worker.js') call. On '/', active manifest = /manifest.json, service worker registers and controls the page. On '/mof30', App.js switches active manifest to /manifest-mof30.json (verified in DOM). Admin login (admin/Admin@12345) succeeds and redirects to /dashboard. /settings renders the install section 'تثبيت / تحديث «إدارة الحسابات»' with install button and shows current admin email as allowed ('مسموح'). Service worker's /api/ network-only rule does NOT break API calls (login worked, dashboard loaded, /api/settings returns 401 as expected). InstallPromptBanner is wired via PublicOrder.jsx but does not appear in headless Chromium since beforeinstallprompt is engagement-gated (per request note: not a failure). No JS runtime errors observed on any route.
critical_code_review_comments: service-worker.js uses cache name 'jawad-v3' with skipWaiting+clients.claim - good. Consider bumping cache name on any icon/manifest change to force refresh (currently OK).
index.html registers SW inside window 'load' handler with silent .catch() - fine. Registration confirmed working in preview (HTTPS).
context_for_next_testing_agent: PWA is fully installable. Assets: /manifest.json (name GAWAD NET, start_url /, standalone, 192+512 icons), /manifest-mof30.json (name إدارة الحسابات, start_url /mof30, standalone), /service-worker.js, /icons/icon-192.png, /icons/icon-512.png all HTTP 200. Manifest link switches via setActiveManifest in App.js based on route. SW registers and controls both routes. InstallPromptBanner presence not verifiable in headless (beforeinstallprompt not fired) - this is expected and NOT a bug per review_request. API calls pass through SW unaffected (network-only for /api/*). The only console message on / was a benign 404 for a bare /api/ probe (no root API endpoint exists); real endpoints like /api/settings respond 401 auth-required correctly.
